llm.summary: The skill is a legitimate ThinkForce mission-management guide, but it gives agents broad mission, credential, browser, and public-sharing authority with insufficient controls for sensitive content.

dimensions.detail: Use of ThinkForce APIs, browsers, E2B sandboxes, Firebase public URLs, and third-party media vendors is partly purpose-aligned, but public long-lived URLs for authenticated dashboard screenshots and raw credential-backed API calls are broader than necessary by default.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package inspected is a Markdown-only skill guide with no executable installer, bundled scripts, or hidden install-time persistence.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions include read-before-write and confirmation for destructive actions, but also describe platform-wide credential discovery, forced continuation after credential retrieval, default raw E2B run_code for integrations, and canonical public upload of authenticated screenshots without a required confirmation or redaction step.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill documents persistent schedules, webhook-triggered subtasks, memory debriefs, collaboration invites, and long-lived public storage; some are disclosed, but public artifacts and credential use lack clear expiration, scoping, and user approval requirements.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Managing missions and subtasks is coherent with the stated purpose, but the documented authority includes running agents, scheduling/webhooks, mission deletion, sharing/invites, stored credential retrieval, browser automation, public uploads, and forwarding artifacts to external vendors.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing if your missions may touch customer data, internal dashboards, paid vendor APIs, or stored credentials. Require users to approve credential use, public sharing, authenticated screenshots, public uploads, destructive mission changes, and external vendor forwarding, and prefer private or expiring URLs over long-lived public links.
llm.findings:
[T09] unexpected: Accepted as a material concern: SKILL.md documents logging into dashboards, screenshotting authenticated pages, uploading them with upload_public, and forwarding long-lived public URLs to vendors without mandatory redaction, expiration, or immediate user approval.
[T05] unexpected: Accepted as a material concern: the platform preamble tells agents to list stored credentials, retrieve credentials before third-party API calls, continue after retrieval, and prefer general-purpose E2B run_code for integrations.
[TM1] expected: The DELETE and revoke endpoints are expected for a mission-management API guide; the skill also says to confirm destructive actions, although the bulk revoke variant still deserves careful use.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Partially accepted: external API keys, stored credentials, public sharing, public uploads, and third-party vendors are disclosed in the body, but the skill lacks a prominent upfront privacy and data-sharing warning.
[EA2] expected: Downgraded for the cited lines: 'Never ask' refers to resolving companyId from the API key, not bypassing user approval; destructive actions are explicitly listed as requiring confirmation.
[P9] expected: Downgraded after inspection: the flagged whitespace appears to be Markdown table formatting/malformed table text, and no hidden off-screen instruction block was found.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted as a quality/safety concern: the guide correctly says agents use enabledTools[] but later tells agents to inspect tools[], which could cause incorrect tool matching.
[P4] expected: Downgraded: preferring lifecycle pause/cancel endpoints over raw status PATCH is purpose-aligned operational guidance, not hidden behavior manipulation.
[PE2] expected: Downgraded: the sudo mention is a sandbox package-install note for E2B and not an install-time privilege escalation mechanism in this skill.
